title: Coefficient comparison
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $k$ is a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\ell\ne p$ is prime, and $X,Y$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $A\to B$ be a map of finite commutative rings, each annihilated by a power of $\ell$.
For $T=X,Y$ and $R=A,B$, write $\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$ for bounded complexes of $R_T$-module sheaves with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Subscripts $B$ denote derived extension of coefficients [sk-def-sp-scalar-extension]. Use the compact-support functors and their constructible right adjoints $Rf_{!,R}\dashv f_R^!$, whose adjunctions on these categories are supplied by [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation].

For $M\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ and $K\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ there are isomorphisms, natural in $M$ and $K$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
b(M)&:(Rf_{!,A}M)_B\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } Rf_{!,B}(M_B)
&&\text{in }\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},B),\\
c_{A,B}(K)&:(f_A^!K)_B\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }f_B^!(K_B)
&&\text{in }\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},B).
\end{aligned}
$$
Here $b$ is the canonical comparison obtained by commuting extension of coefficients past extension by zero and proper direct image in one compactification. The map $c_{A,B}(K)$ is uniquely determined by
$$
\varepsilon_B(K_B)\circ Rf_{!,B}\bigl(c_{A,B}(K)\bigr)
=(\varepsilon_A(K))_B\circ b(f_A^!K)^{-1},
$$
where $\varepsilon_R:Rf_{!,R}f_R^!\to\mathrm{id}$ is the counit of the indicated adjunction for $R=A,B$.

proof.text: Write $T_X=(-)_B$ and $T_Y=(-)_B$ on the two sites, and $F_R=Rf_{!,R}$, $G_R=f_R^!$ for $R=A,B$. By [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], $T_X,T_Y$ are functors preserving $\Dctf$, even when $B$ has infinite projective dimension over $A$. By [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation], $G_AK$ and $G_B(K_B)$ lie in the stated constructible finite-Tor categories and $F_R\dashv G_R$ restricts to these categories. Thus all the objects and adjunction transposes below have the required domains.

Use the chosen compactification $c_f=(X\xrightarrow{j}\bar X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y)$ supplied by [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], with $j$ open and $\bar f$ proper. This is the compactification already used to define $F_A$ and $F_B$; it depends on $f$, not the coefficient ring. Apply [det-sp-reduction-direct-image] to this compactification and $M$. Its displayed comparison gives $b(M):T_YF_AM\xrightarrow{\sim}F_BT_XM$, natural in $M$ and in $\Dctf(Y,B)$. Its explicit absence of a flatness or finite-projective-dimension assumption applies to the arbitrary map $A\to B$ here. This reuses the existing node for the resolution-and-finite-window argument of the blueprint's first paragraph.

proof.text: For $K$ form $\tau_K=T_Y(\varepsilon_A(K))\circ b(G_AK)^{-1}:F_BT_XG_AK\to T_YK$. The bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(F_BN,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(N,G_BL)$ furnished by the adjunction in [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation], with $N=T_XG_AK$ and $L=T_YK$, defines a unique $c_K:T_XG_AK\to G_BT_YK$. The inverse of this bijection sends $h$ to $\varepsilon_B(L)\circ F_B(h)$, so its defining equality is precisely the required counit identity. Thus uniqueness is uniqueness of the transpose; it does not assert that mates of arbitrary isomorphisms are isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, first sentence; detail sk-lem-sp-reduction-exceptional.proof.md, Existence, uniqueness, naturality

proof.text:
For $u:K\to L$, expand $\tau$ from Step 3. Naturality of $\varepsilon_A$ and of $b$ in [det-sp-reduction-direct-image] gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
T_Y(u)\circ\tau_K
&=T_Y(u\circ\varepsilon_A(K))\circ b(G_AK)^{-1}\\
&=T_Y(\varepsilon_A(L))\circ T_YF_AG_A(u)\circ b(G_AK)^{-1}\\
&=T_Y(\varepsilon_A(L))\circ b(G_AL)^{-1}\circ F_BT_XG_A(u)\\
&=\tau_L\circ F_BT_XG_A(u).
\end{aligned}
$$
Under the adjunction of [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation], the inverse transpose of $G_BT_Y(u)\circ c_K$ is
$$
\varepsilon_B(T_YL)\circ F_B(G_BT_Y(u)\circ c_K)
=T_Y(u)\circ\varepsilon_B(T_YK)\circ F_B(c_K)
=T_Y(u)\circ\tau_K,
$$
using naturality of $\varepsilon_B$. The inverse transpose of $c_L\circ T_XG_A(u)$ is
$$
\varepsilon_B(T_YL)\circ F_B(c_L\circ T_XG_A(u))
=\tau_L\circ F_BT_XG_A(u).
$$
The preceding equality and injectivity of the adjunction bijection prove $G_BT_Y(u)\circ c_K=c_L\circ T_XG_A(u)$, the naturality of $c$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, naturality of the transpose; detail sk-lem-sp-reduction-exceptional.proof.md, Existence, uniqueness, naturality

proof.text: Finally apply the existing [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] with this smooth $f$, the finite $\ell$-primary rings $A,B$, and $K$. Its morphism is defined as the transpose of the identical map $T_Y(\varepsilon_A(K))\circ b(G_AK)^{-1}$, using the same compact-support comparison. Uniqueness in Step 3 therefore identifies that morphism with $c_K$. The cited node states that this morphism is an isomorphism (and identifies it on coordinate charts with $(e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d])_B\simeq e^*p_d^*(K_B)(d)[2d]$). Consequently the $c_K$ constructed here is an isomorphism in $\Dctf(X,B)$. This is the existing chart-comparison lemma, not an inference that invertible $b$ alone implies invertible $c$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, chart comparison; existing detail sk-lem-sp-reduction-exceptional.md, isomorphism and chart clauses
